originalPrompts: Individual original generation prompts were not saved in the repository. These replacement prompts were reconstructed from the manuscript, the shared style guide, the existing illustrations, and the indexed reference photographs.

images.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: corrected 16:9 watercolor autobiography illustration. Correct FACE IDENTITY and WATERCOLOR STYLE in input image 5 while keeping its successful scene, composition and physical actions. Reference roles: image 1 is the actual protagonist's face, the adult man in the center of the photograph, with the highest identity priority. Image 2 is the existing approved portrait of the same man. Image 3 is another existing watercolor scene, the father giving his daughter bus fare. Image 4 is the newly corrected binder illustration, an additional face and paint-style continuity anchor. Image 5 is the EDIT TARGET; take its layout and actions, not the current father's generic face or photographic surface.
The protagonist MUST be unmistakably the actual adult man in image 1 and the SAME person as the existing portrait in image 2 and father in image 3. Preserve his face width-to-height, broad midface and full cheeks, softly hooded narrow eyes and familiar brows, broad rounded nose, characteristic lip shape, rounded jaw and chin, ears and forehead-to-hairline relationship. Use age adjustments only for wrinkles and hair; do not redesign facial structure or substitute a generic rural man. No pasted photographic face: paint his real likeness coherently in watercolor. Only the main father's identity is corrected; do not give his face to other family members or neighbors.
Depict the same father in his thirties in this 1960s Anmyeondo scene: modestly soften age lines and keep black hair, but preserve recognizability over aggressive rejuvenation. Keep his head's current three-quarter angle, natural focused expression, padded grey-blue cotton work clothes, and both hands holding the edges of one small straw seaweed drying screen. Keep his wife beside the wooden water tub and mould, the child carrying one screen at waist height, the sloping wooden drying rack with supported separate screens, the coastal courtyard, winter clothes, snow patches and distant tidal flats. Preserve their body positions and natural grounded feet. His wife and child keep their current distinct identities. Maintain credible screen size and continuous fingers/wrists, no hand touching the seaweed itself.
Paint the ENTIRE scene as hand-painted watercolor in the same series as the existing painted references: warm cold-pressed paper, clearly visible translucent washes, soft wet-on-wet transitions, pigment blooms and granulation, broken brush-shaped marks, light paper left in highlights, and lost edges with selective crisp strokes for essential faces, hands and objects. Use broader painted color masses in clothing and background instead of photographic microdetail. The visible texture should come from watercolor pigment and paper, not a uniform noisy filter on a photograph. Keep the series' muted ochre, straw and grey-blue palette and legible realistic anatomy. Avoid glossy rendered skin, sharp photorealism, uniformly stippled digital texture, oil impasto, flat cartoons and hard outlines.
Invariants: 16:9 landscape, same framing, same people and number of hands, same coast, same physically supported rack and sensible screen-handling corrections. Change only the protagonist's likeness and the painting treatment throughout the image. Do not add objects, change body proportions, reintroduce a giant seaweed wall, enlarge the screens, copy the suits or child from the portrait, or add text, logo or watermark.
